examples.knowledge_point: Estimating a Derivative Given a Graph Using a Backward Difference Approximation: Word Problem
examples.problem:
A factory produces fans. The total cost of producing $x$ fans, in dollars, is given by the function $C(x).$  The graph of $C(x)$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14058551/assets/ad3fae3694c4df8269be9a54350aabf83368b3152ea69eb2b9d1ac76e702823f.png)

Approximate the marginal cost $C'(x)$ at the point $x=3$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=2.$
examples.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
C'(x) \approx \dfrac{C(x) - C(x-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $x=3.$ Applying the above formula with $x=3$ and $h=2$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{′}(3) & ≈\frac{C(3)-C(3-2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{C(3)-C(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{30-20}{2} \\  & =\frac{10}{2} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

So the marginal cost is $\[math]5$ per fan.

feedback.problem:
The battery charge of a delivery drone, measured in percent, is given by the function $B(t)$, where $t$ is the time, in hours, since the drone was fully charged. The values of $B(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| $t$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $B(t)$ | $80$ | $72$ | $55$ | $40$ | $35$ |

Approximate the rate of change of the battery charge when $t=6$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

The estimated rate of change when $t=6$ is
{{field-1}} percent per hour.
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{B}^{′}(t)≈\frac{B(t)-B(t-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the time $t=6.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{′}(6) & ≈\frac{B(6)-B(6-2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{B(6)-B(4)}{2} \\  & =\frac{40-55}{2} \\  & =\frac{-15}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the estimated rate of change when $t=6$ is $-\frac{15}{2}$ percent per hour.
